properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued October 30 at 1:57AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
At 157 AM MST, Doppler radar was tracking a line of strong
thunderstorms extending from near Desert Mountain to near Goldfield,
or extending from 9 miles north of Scottsdale to 6 miles north of
Apache Junction, moving northeast at 20 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 30 mph and half inch size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Mesa, Scottsdale, Apache Junction, Fountain Hills, Sugarloaf
Mountain, Ballantine Trailhead, Round Valley, Carefree, Rio Verde,
Goldfield Ranch, McDowell Mountain Park, Saguaro Lake, Salt River
Tubing Recreation Area, Granite Reef Dam, Usery Mountain Park,
Canyon Lake, Goldfield, Lost Dutchman State Park, Four Peaks and
Desert Mountain.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with these storms and may lead
to flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.
properties.area: Cave Creek/New River; New River Mesa; Rio Verde/Salt River; Fountain Hills/East Mesa; Apache Junction/Gold Canyon; Mazatzal Mountains; Pinal/Superstition Mountains

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 29 at 9:03PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds and downstream tidal effects on the St
John River are slowing flow at Astor, which is also impacting river
levels upstream near Deland.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland, Astor...Minor to Moderate
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and forecast to continue.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with
several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals.
Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely
submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Thursday the stage was 3.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EDT Thursday was 3.8 feet.
- Forecast...At Astor, river levels are forecast to slowly decline
but remain in Moderate Flood Stage for at least the next couple
weeks. Additional rises are possible as onshore winds
periodically increase and slow river flow.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Friday afternoon at noon EDT.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream and localized urban flooding caused by
excessive rainfall is possible.


* WHERE...Seward.

* WHEN...Until 415 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Excessive rainfall may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris. Flooding
may occur in poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Light rainfall will gradually increase in intensity this evening
and continue through Friday morning before the rain slowly tapers
off Friday afternoon. Rainfall rates of up to a quarter of an
inch per hour are possible between 10 PM tonight and 10 AM
Friday, with a storm total between 3 and 4 inches of rain likely
with this event. Prolonged heavy rain may lead to areas of
flooding along smaller streams and creeks, in low-lying and poor
drainage areas, and ponding of water on roadways.


- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
